QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_50

question.text: An investor purchases a bond with face value Rs.100, coupon rate 12% per annum, and the bond is currently trading at Rs.109.50 in the market. What is the current yield of this bond?

explanation.text: The Logic: Current yield = Annual coupon / Market price = (12 / 109.50) x 100 = 10.95% (as calculated in the NISM workbook). Since the bond is trading above face value (at a premium), the current yield is LOWER than the coupon rate. The coupon remains Rs.12 annually, but the investor paid Rs.109.50, so the yield on investment is less than 12%. The Trap: 12% (option B) is the coupon rate, not the current yield -- a common mistake. 9.13% (option C) might result from dividing market price by coupon. 14.6% (option D) might result from an incorrect formula inversion. Note: This exact example (12% coupon, Rs.109.50 price, 10.95% current yield) is from the NISM XII workbook (page 73).
